title: Micron Stock (MU) Rises 11.9% After CoreWeave Results (Nov 11)
summary: Micron (MU) closed at $811.30 on Nov 11, up 11.89%, as CoreWeave's Q3 results lifted memory stocks and Anthropic named Micron in its IPO placement.
body_markdown:
## Why Micron Stock Rose


Financial media tied the rally mainly to news from outside Micron. CoreWeave reported its[third-quarter results](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/after-hot-cpi-coreweave-and-costco-tonight/) on Tuesday, and according to[Benzinga](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/micron-sandisk-soar-coreweave-ceo-212511602.html) , memory stocks rallied on Wednesday because the numbers eased fears that AI infrastructure spending was slowing. Benzinga reported that CoreWeave's quarterly revenue rose 168% to $3.66 billion, its backlog reached $132.5 billion and it raised the lower end of its annual capital spending forecast to $37 billion.


Speaking to CNBC on Wednesday, CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator said "the demand for the infrastructure is and remains overwhelming," as cited by Benzinga, which added that CoreWeave has about 10 times as much demand as its remaining 2027 computing capacity. The rally also followed a sharp selloff in memory stocks the prior week, the outlet noted.


Micron also had news of its own. As reported by[GuruFocus](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/micron-stocks-jump-11-2-165403817.html) , the amended filing for[Anthropic's initial public offering](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-opens-retail-allocation-australia-offering-up-to-20-retail/) named Micron for a $1 billion allocation in the concurrent private placement, or 13,513,513 shares at the $74 midpoint. GuruFocus linked Wednesday's move to both the CoreWeave results and the Anthropic allocation.


## MU Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Micron's fiscal fourth-quarter 2026 revenue reached $54.23 billion, up 379.3% from a year earlier, with a gross margin of 87.0%, and the company guided fiscal first-quarter 2027 revenue to $61.5 billion, plus or minus $1.5 billion, per[24/7 Wall St.](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/jim-cramer-says-micron-isn-220724994.html)
- Benzinga noted that Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra said on the September earnings call that more than 75% of Micron's 2027 output was already committed, and that he expects demand to exceed supply in 2027 and 2028.
- Benzinga also cited TrendForce forecasts for conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 10% to 15% in the fourth quarter and NAND flash prices to rise 15% to 20%.


### Risks


- Benzinga said sustaining the rebound depends on whether data-center operators can finance and complete their infrastructure.
- The prior week's memory selloff came after midterm results raised fears that a Democratic-controlled Congress could slow data-center construction, according to Benzinga.
- Memory is cyclical: 24/7 Wall St. noted that Micron's Idaho fab should produce first wafers in mid-calendar 2027, and pricing power could fade as new supply arrives.
